AbstractText.Label: AIMS AND OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effects of empowerment case management on the physical health of Type 2 diabetic patients.

AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Diabetes is a global health issue. Case management is often used on diabetes management at various levels. Empowerment has been used for chronic situation management, but its effects have not been widely studied in diabetic populations.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Purposive sampling was used to recruit 125 participants with type 2 diabetes aged 18 years or older from a regional teaching hospital in Taiwan.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Empowerment case management (ECM) was applied for 42 participants, while the other 83 received normal case management. Survey items included demographics, preprandial (AC) and postprandial (PC) blood sugar levels, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1C), systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) blood pressure, total cholesterol (TC), and the presence or absence of acute and chronic complications. Descriptive statistics and a generalized estimating equation were used to analyze the model's effects on the two groups.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The PC blood sugar levels of patients receiving ECM declined at three months (B=-34.26,p<.01), and this decrease was maintained at six months (B=-83.66, p<.001). As of six months after starting the intervention, patients receiving ECM enjoyed better physical health. These patients' AC blood sugar levels (B=-50.16, p<.001), HbA1C (B=-0.98, p<.001), SBP (B=-8.24, p<.001), DBP (B=-5.73, p<.01), and TC (B=-13.74, p<.05) all experienced a continuous drop and were controlled well, and no diabetes-related acute or chronic complications were observed either. Type 2 diabetic patients who received ECM managed their physical health better. Moreover, its greatest effect was that patients were able to form exercise groups and continue to maintain their health.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: ECM was shown to have a substantial effect on the physical health and self-care of diabetic patients, thus making it a suitable intervention tool for managing diabetes cases. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
